title: Cream of Mushroom Soup
subtitle: Rich blended mushroom soup with a splash of cream
excerpt: Chestnut and button mushrooms sweated with shallots and garlic, deglazed with dry sherry, blended smooth, and finished with a little cream. Deep and earthy, best with a good crusty roll.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cream of mushroom soup achieves its depth by cooking the mushrooms long enough for their liquid to evaporate and for them to begin to colour: this concentrates the earthy, savoury flavour. Dry sherry or Madeira adds another layer of complexity. A small amount of dried porcini soaked in boiling water and added to the stock deepens the flavour considerably but is optional.

recipeTools.notes: For blending directly in the pot.

content.text: Cook the mushrooms in batches if the pan is crowded: overcrowding steams them instead of browning. The colour you develop on the mushrooms at the start is the foundation of the soup's flavour. Do not rush this step.

items.preparation: plus a little extra to serve

content.text: Melt the butter in a large wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10 to 12 minutes until the mushrooms have released their liquid and it has evaporated. The mushrooms should be golden at the edges.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the shallots and garlic and cook for 3 minutes until soft. Add the thyme sprigs. Pour in the sherry and let it bubble for 1 minute, scraping up any browned bits from the base of the pan.
Pour in the hot stock. Simmer for 10 minutes. Remove the thyme stalks. Blend until very smooth. Return to the pan, stir in the cream, and reheat gently. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle into warmed bowls. Swirl a little extra cream over the surface of each bowl. Serve with crusty bread.
